model.name: Deploy-hardening: scripted deploy + served!=committed monitor + pinned prod topology (NEXT, not-now)
model.description: ★ NEXT / NOT-NOW (do NOT dispatch build now - R31.12 is the active item; PO schedules). The recurring PUSH-vs-SERVE deploy lag is a real gap: a commit is pushed but the prod-serving process keeps running the OLD build until a MANUAL Ctrl-C + npm start - there is no auto rebuild+reload, so served != committed until someone notices and restarts by hand. This is the OPERATIONAL COMPLEMENT to the R31.7/R31.13 clean-deploy pair (R31.7 single-source VERSION + R31.13 reproducible BUILD = the ARTIFACT is clean; R31.14 = the DEPLOY actually SERVES that artifact). Three parts: (a) a SCRIPTED deploy = pull + build + VERIFY served==committed==SW==HEAD (no manual Ctrl-C+npm start); (b) a STANDING served!=committed MONITOR - the R31.7 agreement invariant run as a LIVE ALERT so any lag is visible IMMEDIATELY, not discovered by a stale page; (c) PINNED prod TOPOLOGY - exactly ONE prod-serving checkout + exactly ONE restart-driver (architect); the expert commits to a CLONE and does NOT deploy (no ambiguity about who/what serves). Route (when scheduled): architect designs the deploy script + monitor + topology, expert implements, tester gates (push -> scripted deploy -> served==committed within N s; monitor fires on an injected skew). Chain wires onto the built fix. Architect-flagged runbook gap (team-discovery), not a Tron quote.

model.crossRefNote: R31.7 single-source version + R31.13 deterministic build = the clean-deploy ARTIFACT (served==committed==tree-clean by construction). R31.14 = the DEPLOY MECHANISM that guarantees the serving process actually runs that artifact (scripted deploy + live monitor + pinned topology). Together = a fully-closed clean-deploy loop: build clean -> serve clean -> alert if ever skewed. ★ EXTENDED 2026-09-05 (PO route A, the served==committed mint): activated + 5 evidence instances + 4 failable ACs (served-must-be-verified NET-NEW / client-half-now-scheduled folds R40.76 / carries-measured-values / authorized-but-unbuilt=no-invariant). crossRef R30.28 (ship-time guarantee it rides, INV-D6) + R40.76 (client-half, now folded/scheduled) + R40.91 (the two-source-drift law a parallel guard would violate = why we EXTEND not mint) + R40.25 (device-gate served-but-unverified, now HARD-refuse) + R40.54 (satisfaction-fail-closed). check-before-create caught this: the invariant already existed; the gap was activation, not a missing requirement.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A SCRIPTED deploy exists: one command does pull + build + VERIFY served==committed==SW==HEAD, replacing the manual Ctrl-C + npm start. After it runs, the prod-serving process is running the JUST-committed build (no stale old-build lag). If any of served/committed/SW/HEAD disagree, the script FAILS LOUD (does not silently serve stale).

A STANDING served!=committed MONITOR runs continuously (the R31.7 agreement invariant as a LIVE ALERT): if the served version/hash ever diverges from committed==HEAD (i.e. a push happened but the serve didn't reload), it ALERTS IMMEDIATELY - the lag is visible at once, not found later via a stale page. Testable: inject a skew (commit without redeploy) -> the monitor fires.

Prod topology is PINNED: exactly ONE prod-serving checkout and exactly ONE restart-driver (architect). The expert commits to a CLONE and does NOT deploy - no ambiguity about which checkout serves or who restarts. Prevents the 'someone else's checkout served an old/other build' class of lag/confusion.
BUILD-AUTHORIZED (2026-08-10) under Tron's standing campaign directive (finish S30++ tasks -> QA); chain minted scenario-first before the expert lands scripts/deploy.mjs. (Was NEXT/NOT-NOW.)

INV-D1: gate-by-construction — there is NO exit-0 path that ships without the post-deploy device-gate having run GREEN. This is the property that UN-BLOCKS R40.25's AC-8 (the gate stops being skippable). Enforced BOTH ways: a behavioural META-BITE (a normal deploy CANNOT complete un-gated — covers existing paths) AND a STATIC LINT (every exit-0 downstream of the gate — prevents future ones); the lint carries two bites: plant-a-bypass -> RED, and lint-itself-runs -> RED (non-vacuous).

INV-D2: NO skip/bypass flag EVER. There is no --force / --skip-gate / env override. Shipping un-gated is only ever RECORDED as served-but-UNVERIFIED (R40.25), never silenceable. (Prohibition written into the requirement so a future agent does not add a bypass.)
INV-D3: atomic + fail-loud — the deploy never half-completes; on any step failure it fails LOUD and leaves the previous live state intact, never a partial/broken serve.
INV-D4: exactly ONE deploy path when done — no divergent manual vs scripted routes; the scripted path is THE path.
INV-D5: dry-run FIRST, and the EXISTING restart path stays available until the scripted deploy has succeeded >=1 time live (safe cutover, no big-bang).

INV-D6: served==committed comparison RIDES R30.28 (b6946e59.assertVersionAtHead) — NOT a second copy. Distinct intent: R30.28 is the ship-time GUARANTEE; R31.14 is orchestration + drift MONITOR + pinned topology.

What is SERVED must have been VERIFIED. Deploying an UNVERIFIED fix onto prod is a DEFECT, not merely 'recorded as unverified' — 0.8.180 was an unverified fix shipped onto a working-with-a-hole prod and made it STRICTLY WORSE. BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE DEFECTS: committed-but-not-served AND served-but-not-verified. Strengthens R40.25/INV-D2 from 'record served-but-unverified' to 'a deploy whose device-gate has not run GREEN is REFUSED, fail-loud' (the un-verified path does not reach prod).

gateRef.ref: deploy gate (rides R40.25 device-gate, made a HARD refuse)
gateRef.assertion: a deploy of a version whose device-gate has not run GREEN is REFUSED (fail-loud), never served-then-recorded

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING: seed a deploy of an un-gated/unverified version -> RED/refused

acceptanceCriteria.text: The served==committed guard covers BOTH halves — the SERVER version AND the CLIENT loaded-bundle marker: a source-only client commit does NOT ship until dist is rebuilt AND served, and the guard MEASURES the served client bundle marker independently of the server version. Folds R40.76 (client-half coverage gap) in as NOW-SCHEDULED, not deferred — instance E1 (4-round hunt) is precisely this gap biting.

gateRef.assertion: served client bundle marker == committed client source; a source-only client change not rebuilt+served => RED (looks-shipped-but-isnt)

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING: seed a source-only client commit with stale dist -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: The guard/monitor output CARRIES the MEASURED values — served version, committed version (HEAD), and the client loaded-bundle marker — as evidence, NOT a bare pass/fail (same evidence-not-boolean discipline as R31.7 single-source version + R40.91 measured guard). A user/agent can read the three numbers and see the skew directly.

gateRef.assertion: monitor emits {servedVersion, committedVersion, clientBundleMarker}; a bare-boolean output with no measured values => RED

acceptanceCriteria.stubMustFail: PENDING: seed a values-less boolean monitor -> RED

acceptanceCriteria.text: An AUTHORIZED-BUT-UNBUILT invariant is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NO INVARIANT (PO finding: R31.14 build-authorized 2026-08-10, never activated, so today's 4 committed-not-served fixes went uncaught). This requirement is NOT satisfied until the monitor/gate is OBSERVABLY RUNNING (heartbeat + CI asserts liveness), never merely 'authorized' or 'built'. Same satisfaction-fail-closed discipline as R40.54; same meta-pattern as committed-but-not-served (a thing that exists but does not RUN is not shipped).

gateRef.assertion: the served!=committed monitor is observably RUNNING (recent heartbeat) and CI asserts it; monitor-authorized-but-not-running => RED
